compound-stability-existing-rules.note: Universal fairness/action conjuncts distinguish the first entry. The next two cover overlapping always-conjunction goals with different available helpers; neither excludes the other. The extra-wrapper entry is a specific failed-call diagnosis, not a required stage.

always-conjunction-per-conjunct-stabilit.title: Always-conjunction with pairwise stability helpers
always-conjunction-per-conjunct-stabilit.when: The target is a left-nested conjunction of always predicates and matching always/conjunction helpers are available
always-conjunction-per-conjunct-stabilit.avoid: Unavailable helpers or incompatible predicate shapes/nesting

existing-stabilization-proof-object-lift.title: Always-conjunction with a local proof object or macro
existing-stabilization-proof-object-lift.when: The target is a finite always-lifted conjunction and a matching local proof object or macro accepts its lifted arguments
existing-stabilization-proof-object-lift.avoid: Absent/incompatible proof objects or wrong predicate lifting level

direct-existing-lemma-bridge.note: 003 and 043 have different premise-to-goal directions. The library-lemma entry is a general option and may also match either case; it is not a third mutually exclusive goal. Constructor fallback remains conditional in the original specialized bodies.

scope_replacements.old: - Consult when: Goal is a known property about library types or structured view equality
scope_replacements.new: - Consult when: A library lemma matches an algebraic goal, or the goal connects serialization, view equality, and marshalability

scope_replacements.old: - Consult when: An installed or already-declared lemma/trait contract has matching conclusion and available premises
scope_replacements.new: - Consult when: The selected direct route has a matching installed/declared lemma or trait contract with available premises

scope_replacements.old:
- Not for: No matching lemma or extra premises are unavailable
- Not for: Equality form cannot connect to current postcondition
- Not for: Manual constructor case is required because bridge is insufficient
scope_replacements.new:
- Not for the direct route: Its matching lemma, premises, or required equality connection are unavailable
- Boundary: Cards 003/043 also describe conditional constructor fallbacks; failure of a direct bridge does not exclude those original fallback cases

original-card-003.title: Marshalable + equal serialization to equal views
original-card-003.when: Both values are marshalable, serialized representations agree, and an existing trait/instance promises view equality
original-card-003.avoid: Trait unavailable or its view relation cannot imply the required structural equality

original-card-043.title: Equal abstract views to equal marshalability
original-card-043.when: The premise is abstract-view equality and the goal is equality of marshalability predicates
original-card-043.avoid: The goal has a different proof direction; an uninstantiable direct bridge requires the original conditional fallback

eventual-witness-index-bridge.note: 008 starts with eventual action occurrence; 009 already has a raw state witness but lacks the suffix form. 061 covers obtaining a reachability index from an established existential and can overlap witness selection in 008. These are not mandatory successive reads.

finite-set-fold-cardinality-induction.note: Select by the requested conclusion: result finiteness versus equality to the mapped source set. Sharing cardinality induction does not make the conclusions interchangeable.

function-field-projection-syntax.note: 015 covers both method/field directions and a separate antecedent diagnosis; 028 focuses on pointwise record equality; the merged rule focuses on stored-function field calls. Field-call and later trigger cases overlap. These are reading focuses, not exclusive eligibility tests.

scope_replacements.old:
- Consult when: Compile/type error says a public/spec function-valued field is used with call-like dot syntax or a method name is taken as a field
- Consult when: The referenced item is a function-valued struct field
- Not for: The item is an actual declared method
- Not for: The field is not function-valued
scope_replacements.new:
- Consult when: A method is mistaken for a field, a stored function field is called as a method, or pointwise record equality has the related syntax/trigger failure
- Consult when: Card-015's separate case matches a quantified-proof missing-antecedent diagnostic
- Not for: None of these method/field, pointwise-equality trigger, or missing-antecedent diagnostics is present
- Boundary: The stored-function rule excludes genuine methods; that exclusion does not exclude card-015's method-as-field case

card-015-verbatim.title: Method/field classification or separate antecedent issue
card-015-verbatim.when: A method is treated as a field, a function field as a method, or a quantified proof lacks its implication antecedent
card-015-verbatim.avoid: Neither method/field nor antecedent diagnostic is present; implication syntax is version-sensitive

card-028-verbatim.title: Pointwise record equality with function-field diagnostics
card-028-verbatim.when: The failing proof is pointwise record equality and has field-call syntax or uninferred equality-trigger diagnostics
card-028-verbatim.avoid: Treating pointwise agreement as field/record equality before the original rule's field-equality obligation is met

ghost-empty-witness.note: The aggregate entry addresses the returned multi-field ghost witness; the history entry addresses one initializer field constrained by an abstract initial-state relation. A history may be part of an aggregate, so both can match.

loop-termination-and-invariants.note: Choose the current failing obligation: missing decreases, unavailable entry assumptions, or packet-prefix set/validity reasoning. The packet rule also carries pre-loop facts, so it overlaps the assumption rule. The source does not require reading all three in order.

scope_replacements.old: - Consult when: While loop lacks a decreases clause or loop-body assertions/preconditions fail because function-entry assumptions disappear
scope_replacements.new: - Consult when: A while loop lacks decreases, loses entry assumptions in its body, or fails packet-prefix set/validity obligations

scope_replacements.old:
- Not for: Termination is not a simple decreasing numeric measure
- Not for: Relevant assumption is not preserved on every iteration
scope_replacements.new:
- Not for the counting-termination rule: No strictly decreasing numeric measure of the stated form
- Not for carrying an unchanged assumption: It is not preserved on every iteration; this does not exclude the packet rule's evolving inductive relation

packet-prefix-set-invariant.title: Packet-prefix append loop with set/validity failure
packet-prefix-set-invariant.when: After termination repair, a packet-append prefix loop still fails final set equality, invariant preservation, or a match-arm obligation
packet-prefix-set-invariant.avoid: A different loop relation is required; missing element-validity premises still need proof

natural-integer-type-mismatch.note: Distinguish integer-valued predecessor subtraction where a natural is needed from a natural sequence length where an integer is needed. Empty-sequence element inference is a second case in the latter rule. The conversion directions are opposite, not interchangeable.

natural-predecessor-subtraction-conversi.title: Natural predecessor expression: integer to natural mismatch
natural-predecessor-subtraction-conversi.when: A natural-induction helper expects a natural predecessor but subtraction produces an integer
natural-predecessor-subtraction-conversi.avoid: The branch does not establish nonnegativity or safe conversion

empty-sequence-length-annotation.title: Sequence argument: unknown element type or natural to integer mismatch
empty-sequence-length-annotation.when: An empty sequence has unknown element type, or a natural sequence length is supplied to an integer-index interface
empty-sequence-length-annotation.avoid: That type is already known or that interface accepts natural indices

opaque-spec-function-facts.note: 019 concerns rejected fuel reveal on a nondecreasing wrapper. 021 concerns a closed length fact with an open counterpart/connector; 053 is the length-prefixed injectivity case with a fixed-width length/round-trip lemma. Length subgoals can overlap; check which library facts actually exist.

rule-card-021.title: Closed serialization length with an open counterpart
rule-card-021.when: A needed closed-function length fact is unavailable directly but the library has an open counterpart and connector
rule-card-021.avoid: No open counterpart/connector or the spec avoids encoding details

rule-card-053.title: Header/payload injectivity with a fixed-width encoding lemma
rule-card-053.when: Length-prefixed injectivity needs header/sequence facts and the library supplies a fixed-width length and decode-round-trip lemma
rule-card-053.avoid: No fixed-width header or no such installed encoding lemma

post-verification-cleanup.note: After verification, distinguish executable-shape differences, module-scope directives, set-proof imports/macros, and warnings only. Directive and set-import cases may overlap and offer alternatives; a warning-only case is not evidence of a proof repair.

proof-helper-qualified-path.note: The sequence-equality closure entry specializes the general out-of-scope proof-helper route and adds its equality-obligation context. Both may match a sequence helper; choose by the missing item, not by an invented exclusion of sequence cases from the general rule.

quantified-proof-antecedent-binder-scope.note: All three can match a helper failure caused by a missing antecedent. The merged rule surveys that diagnostic; 023 additionally covers a shadowed bound symbol; 074 focuses on a helper call inside the implication. These are overlapping focuses, not three distinct error classes.

missing-antecedent-quantified-proof.title: Missing-antecedent diagnostic: general coverage
missing-antecedent-quantified-proof.when: An inner assertion or lemma fails with a missing-antecedent diagnostic inside a quantified implication
missing-antecedent-quantified-proof.avoid: Antecedent already available, a different premise missing, or a trigger-inference-only failure

quantified-binder-scope-verbatim.title: Missing antecedent with binder/available-bound context
quantified-binder-scope-verbatim.when: A quantified proof cannot use antecedent-dependent bounds/facts; the rule also covers a bound symbol shadowed by a fresh one
quantified-binder-scope-verbatim.avoid: Bounds genuinely absent or no binder/antecedent issue; implication syntax is version-sensitive

helper-precondition-implication-branch-v.title: Missing antecedent at a helper-call precondition
helper-precondition-implication-branch-v.when: A helper inside a quantified implication fails its precondition, or that assertion warns its antecedent is not assumed
helper-precondition-implication-branch-v.avoid: Changing specification requires/ensures, or a goal already discharged by a supplied case lemma

record-function-field-equality.note: 004 addresses the remaining record-equality goal from full pointwise agreement; 005 is explicitly conditioned on direct function equality failing and unavailable/rejected helper names. Distinguish the observed proof state, not two different mathematical premises.

sequence-fold-concat-equality.note: Both address the same concatenated-fold goal. One needs compatible prefix/last decomposition; the other an installed split lemma and compatible accumulator formulation. If both are available, the source does not establish a unique best route or require both.

seq-fold-concat-induction-second.title: Concatenated fold with prefix/last decomposition
seq-fold-concat-induction-second.when: Direct concatenated-fold proof fails and the recursive fold has usable prefix/last decomposition with an append-like accumulator
seq-fold-concat-induction-second.avoid: Incompatible accumulator operation or unavailable decomposition relationship

seq-fold-concat-split-lemma-helper.title: Same concatenated-fold goal with an installed split lemma
seq-fold-concat-split-lemma-helper.when: An installed split lemma matches the concatenation boundary and the accumulator-plus-empty formulation is compatible
seq-fold-concat-split-lemma-helper.avoid: No matching split lemma or incompatible accumulator formulation

set-equality-membership-witness.note: 002 is broadly triggered by set/image equality but its concrete body uses image/union witnesses. 049 specifically needs duplicate-free sequence removal and shifted indices. Select by that structure; do not assume the image-union recipe proves arbitrary set equalities.

rule-general-set-image-equality-witness.title: Set/image equality; concrete image-union witness case
rule-general-set-image-equality-witness.when: Set/image equality lacks a direct lemma and reverse membership fails; the original body develops the image-of-union case
rule-general-set-image-equality-witness.avoid: A matching library lemma already closes the goal; do not assume its image-union details fit a different set operation

temporal-existential-witness-lifting.note: 033 has an equality goal with equality/witness rules. 016 and 032 have leads-to goals and substantially overlapping witness lifting/composition: 016 emphasizes exact message templates, 032 intermediate predicates and final chaining. Neither leads-to entry is exclusive.

scope_replacements.old:
- Consult when: A concrete witness can be selected from an atomic state relation
- Not for: No trusted per-witness lemma exists
- Not for: Witness cannot be selected from atomic membership/state equality
scope_replacements.new:
- For leads-to: Check the selected rule's per-witness helper premises; card-016 also requires an atomic membership/equality witness source
- For equality (card-033): Check the trusted predicate-equality and witness-introduction rules and witness facts; a per-witness leads-to lemma is not its premise
- Not for: The selected rule's required trusted helpers or witness facts are unavailable

card-016-verbatim.title: Existential leads-to: message-template coverage
card-016-verbatim.when: Per-message leads-to lemmas exist but existential state predicates do not connect to their witness-specific templates
card-016-verbatim.avoid: No trusted per-witness lemma or no atomic membership/equality witness source

card-032-verbatim.title: Existential leads-to: intermediate-chain coverage
card-032-verbatim.when: Source/intermediate states are existential but supplied helper lemmas cover individual witnesses
card-032-verbatim.avoid: A needed per-witness helper is absent/uninstantiable; separate legs may still leave the final chain open

card-033-verbatim.title: Existential temporal equality, not just leads-to
card-033-verbatim.when: The goal is equality involving an existential temporal predicate and trusted equality/witness-introduction rules are supplied
card-033-verbatim.avoid: Either required rule or witness facts are unavailable; an unassumed antecedent still needs its own check

temporal-predicate-equality-pointwise.note: 029 concerns moving universal/always operators with matching commutation helpers; 070 concerns one versus two applications of the same operator and the associated index identities. Select by the actual two sides of the equality.

temporal-suffix-shift-helper.note: 014 starts from a nested-always goal and a forward-shift helper. 025 starts from an always-lifted action premise and seeks suffix-wise action satisfaction with an unfolding helper. A larger proof may need both; match the current premise and goal.

transition-system-step-safety.note: 010 covers the outer all-future invariant; 011 a network-multiset update preservation subgoal; 012 the controller's no-external-request subcase. These are proof levels that can be needed together, not rival answers to one identical local obligation.

trigger-inference-annotation.note: 034 focuses on trigger inference only. 018 and 057 also cover independently diagnosed missing antecedents; 018 emphasizes witness/entailment terms, 057 state/suffix terms. An assertion trigger error can match all three. 018 retains a source Action/Validate wording tension; no exclusive split is claimed.

scope_replacements.old: - Consult when: Verus reports it cannot automatically infer triggers for a quantified assertion, choose, or witness term
scope_replacements.new: - Consult when: Verus cannot infer triggers for a quantified assertion, choose, or witness term; cards 018/057 also cover a separately diagnosed missing antecedent

scope_replacements.old: - Not for: Failure is a missing antecedent rather than trigger selection
scope_replacements.new:
- Boundary: A missing-antecedent-only case is not card-034's trigger-only case; it remains within cards 018/057's stated coverage
- Not for: A genuinely missing logical premise, rather than trigger selection or antecedent availability

original-card-018.title: Trigger/antecedent coverage with witness or entailment terms
original-card-018.when: Assertion/witness choice has a trigger-inference error or a quantified proof lacks its antecedent; witness/entailment terms are this rule's focus
original-card-018.avoid: Neither diagnostic present or a real premise missing; the source's Action/Validate wording tension remains

original-card-034.title: Trigger-only coverage for assertion or choose
original-card-034.when: Verus cannot infer triggers for a quantified assertion or witness choice
original-card-034.avoid: Only a successful-proof trigger note remains; a missing-antecedent-only case is outside this rule's trigger

original-card-057.title: Trigger/antecedent coverage with state or suffix terms
original-card-057.when: A universal assertion has a trigger-inference error or lacks its implication antecedent; quantified state/suffix terms are this rule's focus
original-card-057.avoid: A new logical premise is needed; warning cleanup after success is not evidence of required proof repair

universal-instantiation-concrete.note: 037 specializes an available sequence fact at an in-bounds index; 058 an available entailment at one execution; 076 stability facts at a recursive helper with alias-sensitive matching. This is fact instantiation, not a general trigger-inference repair.
